claim: Increasing substrate temperature during PECVD growth of vertical graphene nanosheets (VGNs) promotes the transition from a nanographitic layer to three-dimensional vertical sheet structures, increases lateral sheet dimensions, and improves crystalline quality at sufficiently high temperatures, while intermediate temperatures introduce structural defects.
falsifier: The relationship can be tested by growing VGNs via PECVD at a series of substrate temperatures while keeping other parameters constant and characterizing morphology and crystallinity with SEM and Raman spectroscopy.

conditions: Substrate temperature range from below 625°C to 800°C
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported PECVD system, substrate materials, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
